rules.rule: Check for urgent features and signs of occupational stress in the health worker
rules.problem: check_for omits Diagnosis of long-term condition and Frequent lateness from the identify section; 'past year'/'past month' windows cannot be expressed in check_for (acceptable). Trigger 'Stress at work' is not a common symptom or warning sign, so the task may never fire unless something records it.

rules.rule: Diagnose possible substance misuse in health worker with occupational stress
rules.problem: Requires Stress at work as an AND precondition, but the section is "Identify occupational stress": the listed signs are how stress is identified, so a health worker presenting with them but no recorded Stress at work never triggers the rule. Omits page signs "Diagnosis of long-term condition" (Recent distressing event), "Frequent lateness" (Poor attendance) and the "Marked decline in work performance" heading; "any of the above" also arguably includes the red-box features, which are not in the OR list. Possible (not probable) matches "may have"; the any-sign-to-all-four mapping is faithful to the page wording. Time windows (past year / past month) dropped.

rules.rule: Urgent: health worker with occupational stress and intoxication, inappropriate or aggressive behaviour, or suicidal thoughts
rules.problem: Urgent level justified by 'Arrange urgent assessment'; all four red-box bullets covered. Minor: 'at work' context not encoded; 'Violent acts towards others' (finding) is a closer concept for 'violent behaviour' than Physical aggression.

summary: All four diagnosis rules require Stress at work as a precondition, although the page's 'Identify occupational stress' section uses these signs to identify the stress, and they omit 'Diagnosis of long-term condition' and 'Frequent lateness'. The past-year (alcohol/drugs) and past-month (mood) windows are dropped in the diagnosis rules. The red-box urgent rule is sound apart from the missing 'at work' context.
